==English== {{wp}} ===Etymology=== {{ety|en|:inh|enm:not|tree=1}} From {{der|en|enm|not,nat}}, a variant of {{m|enm|noght}}, {{m|enm|naht|t=not, nothing}}, from {{der|en|ang|*nōht,nāht|t=nought, nothing}}, shortening of {{m|ang|nōwiht}}, {{m|ang|nāwiht|t=nothing|lit=not anything}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*naiwwiht}}, corresponding to {{m|ang|ne|t=not}} + {{m|ang|ōwiht}}, {{m|ang|āwiht|t=anything}}, corresponding to {{m|ang|ā|t=ever, always}} + {{m|ang|wiht|t=thing, creature}}. Cognate with {{cog|sco|nat}}, {{m|sco|naucht||not}}, {{cog|stq|nit||not}}, {{cog|fy|net||not}}, {{cog|nl|niet||not}}, {{cog|de|nicht||not}}. Compare {{l|en|nought}}, {{l|en|naught}} and {{l|en|aught}}. More at {{m|en|no}}, {{m|en|wight}}, {{m|en|whit}}. ===Pronunciation=== * {{a|en|UK}} ** {{IPA|en|/nɒt/|a=RP}} ** {{IPA|en|/nɔt/|a=SSB}} * {{IPA|en|/nɑt/|a=GA}} * {{IPA|en|/nɒt/|a=CA}} * {{IPA|en|/nɔt/|a=AU}} * {{IPA|en|/nɒt/|[nɔ̟t]|a=NZ}} * {{IPA|en|[nɞt]|a=Ireland}} ** {{IPA|en|[näʔ]|a=Dublin}} * {{rhymes|en|ɒt|s=1}} * {{audio|en|en-uk-not.ogg|a=UK}} * {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Back ache-not.wav|a=London}} * {{audio|en|en-us-not.ogg|a=US}} * {{hyph|en|not}} * {{hmp|en|knot|;|naught|nought}} ===Adverb=== {{en-adv|-}} # {{n-g|Negates the meaning of the modified verb.}} #: {{ux|en|Did you take out the trash? — No, I did '''not'''. I do '''not''' think it was my turn, was it?}} #: {{ux|en|'''Not''' knowing any better, I went ahead.}} #: {{ux|en|It was felt desirable that she '''not''' leave school before fourteen.}} #: {{ux|en|I'd rather Mom (did) '''not''' stay, [[cuz]] the best thing about a holiday is '''not''' working.}} #: {{ux|en|'''Not''' a day passes when I do'''n't''' regret '''not''' having enrolled in medicine.}} #: {{ux|en|A callback pay for the workers [[called in]] to work when '''not''' scheduled to do so.}} #* '''1973''' November 17, {{w|Richard Milhous Nixon}}, [[:w:I'm not a crook|Orlando press conference]]: #*: People have got to know [[whether]] or '''not''' their [[:w:President of the United States|president]] is a [[crook]]. Well, I'm '''not''' a [[crook]]. I've earned everything I've got. #* {{RQ:Fry Liar|page=42|passage=The sound of {{w|Abba}} singing ‘{{w|Dancing Queen}}’ had started up in a room the other side of the court. Adrian slammed the window shut.
‘That’ll teach you to throw things out of the window,’ said Gary.
‘It’ll teach me '''''not''''' to throw things out of the window.’}} #* '''1998''' January 26, {{w|William Jefferson Clinton}}, [[:w:I did not have sex with that woman|White House press conference]]: # To no degree. #: {{ux|en|That is '''not''' red; it's green.}} #: {{ux|en|[[it's not you, it's me|It's '''not''' you, it's me.]]}} # {{lb|en|litotes}} {{n-g|Used to indicate the opposite or near opposite, often in a form of understatement.}} #: ''That day was '''not''' the best day of my life.'' (meaning the day was bad or awful) #: ''It was '''not''' my favorite movie of all time.'' (meaning the speaker dislikes or strongly dislikes the movie) #: {{ux|en|After '''not''' [[a few]] threats, they got what they’d been after for so long.}} #: {{ux|en|In the '''not''' too distant future my view on the matter might be '''not''' a million miles away from yours.}} #: {{ux|en|I wonder if I should'''n't''' see a doctor - I've been feeling funny the last few days.}} # {{n-g|Used before a [[determiner phrase]], a [[pronominal phrase]] etc. to convey a [[negative]] [[attitude]] (e.g. [[denial]], [[sadness]], [[anger]]) towards something.}} #: {{ux|en|Oh god, '''not''' that! Anything but that!}} #: {{ux|en|'''Not''' another rainy day!}} # {{lb|en|ironic|informal|originally|AAVE}} {{n-g|Used before a {{w|non-finite clause}} (especially a [[gerund]]-[[participial]] clause) or less commonly a [[determiner phrase]] to [[ironically]] convey some [[attitude]] (e.g. [[surprise]], [[incredulity]], [[amusement]]{{,}} or [[embarrassment]]) towards something.}} ≈ [[look at|Look at]]; [[there be|there is]]. {{defdate|attested since the late 2000s, popularized around 2020}}{{cite-web|date=2021-04-11|author=Colin Morris|title=''Not them having a whole zoo''—the rise of ironic "not"|work=colin_morris|titleurl=https://colinmorris.github.io/blog/ironic-not|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20260414223842/https://colinmorris.github.io/blog/ironic-not|archivedate=14 April 2026}}{{cite-journal|en|title=''Not me getting with the times'': A new kind of ''not''-fragment in English|titleurl=https://elischolar.library.yale.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=1013&context=ygdp|author=Guilherme M. C. Pereira|date=2023-12-19|journal=Yale Working Papers in Grammatical Diversity|publisher=Yale University Department of Linguistics|volume=5|issue=1}} #: {{uxi|en|'''Not''' me writing example sentences again.|Oh my, there I go writing example sentences again!}} #* {{RQ:Twitter|en|date=2023-07-08|handle=brielarson|id=1677550622994845702|authorgloss={{w|Brie Larson}}|passage='''Not''' me crying by the end of that!! You are a brilliant, beautiful human who deserves no less than the world. Thank you for taking the time to watch unicorn store. It’s a film that means so much to me.}} #* {{quote-journal|en|date=2023-12-09|title=Keke Palmer and Darius Jackson: A Complete Relationship Timeline|journal=w:[[Glamour (magazine)|Glamour]]|url=https://www.glamour.com/story/keke-palmer-and-darius-jackson-relationship-timeline|passage={{w|Keke Palmer|[Keke] Palmer}} tells {{w|Hoda Kotb}} and {{w|Jenna Bush Hager}} to “mind y'all's business” when they ask about her relationship with [Darius] Jackson. ¶ “'''Not''' y’all trying to get into it! They trying it on the ''Today'' show,” Palmer joked when the subject was first brought up on ''{{w|Today with Hoda & Jenna|Today With Hoda & Jenna}}''.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20260130172302/https://www.glamour.com/story/keke-palmer-and-darius-jackson-relationship-timeline|archivedate=30 January 2026}} ====Usage notes==== In modern usage, [[w:Do-support|''do''-support]] requires that the form ''do not ...'' (or ''don’t ...'') be preferred to ''... not'' for all but a short list of verbs (be, have, can, could, shall, should, will, would, may, might, must, need, ought, dare): * ''They do '''not''' sow.'' (modern) vs. ''They sow '''not'''.'' (KJB) American usage tends to prefer ''don’t have'' or ''haven’t got'' to ''have not'' or ''haven’t'', except when ''have'' is used as an auxiliary (or in the idiom ''have-not''): * ''I don’t have a clue'' or ''I haven’t got a clue.'' (US) * ''I haven’t a clue'' or ''I haven’t got a clue.'' (outside US) * ''I haven’t been to Spain.'' (universal) The verb ''need'' is only directly negated when used as an auxiliary; this usage is rare in the US but common elsewhere. * ''You don’t need to trouble yourself.'' (common in US) * ''You needn’t trouble yourself.'' (common outside US) * ''I don’t need any eggs today.'' (universal) The verb ''dare'' can sometimes be directly negated. * ''I daren't do that.'' The verb ''do'', as a main verb, takes ''do not''. * ''He does not do that.'' In the imperative, all verbs, including ''be'', take ''do not''. * ''Don't do that.'' * ''Don't be silly.'' (not *''Be not silly.'') In the infinitive, verbs must be negated directly. In this case ''not'' cannot appear after the verb; some authorities recommend placing it before ''to'' to avoid a [[w:split infinitive|split infinitive]], but for most speakers the forms ''not to do'' and ''to not do'' are more or less interchangeable, with the latter being mostly informal. * ''The objective is not to lose'' or ''The objective is to not lose.'' * ''I wanted not to go'' or ''I wanted to not go.'' (Note the difference between this and ''I didn't want to go'', where ''want'' is the verb being negated.) In the subjunctive mood, ''do''-support is not used for negation; ''not'' is placed by itself, or with {{m|en|should}}, immediately before the verb it modifies, even ''be'': * ''They suggested that he (should) '''not''' do it.'' * ''The law requires that it (should) '''not''' be done.'' ====Derived terms==== {{col|en|astronot|not much|Not-Deer|injucundity|not dog|not-for-profit|not-self|not-so-hot|notness|notpology|notspot|notwheat|whatnot|wherenot |could not get elected dogcatcher|not a word|not necessarily|not again|not to put too fine a point on it}} '''Not''' and raise two kids.}} ====Usage notes==== * The construction “A, not B” is synonymous with the constructions “A, and not B”; “not B, but A”; and “not B, but rather A”. ====Translations==== {{trans-top|And not}}{{multitrans|data= * Arabic: * Assamese: * Chinese: * Czech: * Dutch: * Estonian: * Finnish: * French: * Galician: * Georgian: * German: * Greek: * Hebrew: * Hungarian: * Icelandic: * Indonesian: * Italian: * Japanese: * Kapampangan: * Kurdish: * Malay: * Middle English: * Norwegian: * Old English: * Persian: * Polish: * Portuguese: * Romanian: * Russian: {{tt|ru|а не}}, {{tt+|ru|не}} * Slovak: * Spanish: * Sundanese: * Swedish: * Tatar: * Turkish: }} {{trans-bottom}} ===Interjection=== {{head|en|interjection|head=not!}} # {{senseid|en|interjection}} {{lb|en|slang}} {{non-gloss|Used to indicate that the previous phrase was meant [[sarcastically]] or [[ironically]].}} {{defdate|chiefly 1990s}} #: {{cot|en|just kidding#Interjection}} #: {{nearsyn|en|I don't think#Interjection|;|psych#Interjection|;|bender#Interjection}} #: {{ux|en|I really like hanging out with my little brother watching ''Barney'' … '''not'''!}} #: {{ux|en|Sure, you’re perfect the way you are … '''not'''!}} #* {{RQ:Grey Young Pitcher|chapter=Out on the Field|page=64|passage=You've got a swell chance to make this [baseball] team, you have, '''''not'''''! Charming place - '''not'''.}} ====Translations==== {{trans-top}}{{multitrans|data= * Chinese: * Danish: * Faroese: * Finnish: * French: * Galician: * Icelandic: * Japanese: * Kapampangan: * Malay: * Norwegian: * Old Norse: * Portuguese: * Swedish: }} {{trans-bottom}} ====See also==== * [[Appendix:American Dialect Society words of the year]] ===Noun=== {{en-noun}} # An [[instance#Noun|instance]] of using the word "not"; a [[negation]] or [[denial]]. # {{alt case|en|NOT|t=unary operation on logical values that changes true to false, and false to true}}. ====Usage notes==== Boolean operators and states are commonly written in all uppercase in order to distinguish them from the ordinary uses of the words. ====Translations==== {{trans-top|unary negation function}}{{multitrans|data= * Finnish: * Kapampangan: * Malay: * Swedish: }} {{trans-bottom}} ===See also=== {{col|en|sort=0 |if |then |else |and |no |or |true |false }} ===References=== {{reflist}} ===Further reading=== * {{R:OneLook}} ===Anagrams=== * {{anagrams|en|a=not|-ton|NTO|ONT|Ont|Ont.|TNO|TON|on't|ton}} {{cln|en|degree adverbs}}
